death.label: Leif Erikson died, c. 1020, probably at Brattahlíð
death.source: Leif Erikson (Wikipedia): no saga records his death
death.text: The sagas are silent. He is last named alive about 1018–19 and his son Thorkell held the chieftaincy by 1025; Brattahlíð, the family estate, is the likeliest place.

death.label: Marco Polo died at Venice, 8 Jan 1324
death.text: He died at home in January 1324. His will freed Peter, his Tatar slave. Priests are said to have urged him on his deathbed to take back his Book; he answered that he had not told the half of what he saw.

death.label: Ibn Battuta died in Morocco, c. 1369
death.text: He dictated the Rihla at Fez in 1355–56 and died in Morocco about 1368–69. Nobody recorded where, so the skull stands in the country, not on a town.

alternatives.label: Died at Marrakesh, by one modern account
alternatives.text: Some modern summaries put his death at Marrakesh; the Rihla ends in 1355 and no chronicle of his death survives. The tomb shown at Tangier, his birthplace, is purported, and marks a burial tradition, not a place of death.
alternatives.source: Wikipedia, Ibn Battuta (infobox); the Tangier tomb is captioned "purported"

death.label: Zheng He died at sea on the way home, 1433
death.source: Zheng He (Wikipedia); no source gives the place
death.text: Most accounts have him die in 1433 on the way home from the seventh voyage, some say buried at sea. None gives a place, so the skull stands mid-way along that voyage's Calicut–Malacca leg.

alternatives.label: Died at Calicut on the way home, 1433
alternatives.text: On the seventh voyage the fleet called at Calicut on its way back from Hormuz. Some historians have him die there, before it sailed for Malacca.

alternatives.label: Home at Nanjing, died 1435
alternatives.text: A minority view, from later texts and inscriptions, has him live two years more. A tomb is shown at Nanjing.
alternatives.source: Zheng He (Wikipedia); the later Nanjing account

death.label: Dias lost in a storm off the Cape, on Cabral's fleet, 1500
death.text: Four of Cabral's ships went down in one storm on the way to the Cape. The wreck's position is not recorded; the skull stands off the Cape.

death.label: Columbus dies at Valladolid
death.text: He died in a rented house, ill, still arguing that the Crown owed him the titles and the tenth of the profits it had promised. He is generally said to have held that he had reached the edge of Asia. His bones were carried to Seville, then Santo Domingo, then Havana, then Seville again, and Seville and Santo Domingo both still claim him.

death.label: Paulo da Gama died at Angra, Terceira
death.text: Paulo commanded the São Rafael, burned on the East African coast when there were too few men left to sail her. He fell ill on the way home; Vasco sailed on ahead in a fast caravel, to hurry him to the Azores, and stayed with his brother until he died.

death.label: Vasco da Gama died at Cochin as Viceroy of India
death.text: Sent back to India at last as viceroy, he fell ill within months of landing and died at Cochin on Christmas Eve. His body was taken to Portugal in 1539, and lies today in the Jerónimos Monastery at Lisbon.

death.label: Magellan killed at Mactan
death.text: Magellan took sides in a local quarrel, for the Cebu king against Lapulapu of Mactan, and went ashore with about fifty men. The ships' guns could not reach the beach, the Mactan fighters came on in waves, and the captain-general was killed in the water. Pigafetta, who was there, called him "our mirror, our light, our comfort and our true guide".

death.label: Elcano died at sea on the Loaísa expedition, 1526
death.text: He took command when Loaísa died days before, and died himself at sea on 4 August. No position is recorded; the skull is a guess in the middle of the Pacific.

death.label: Drake died off Portobelo, 1596; buried at sea in a lead coffin
death.text: Dysentery killed him on his last raid on the Spanish Caribbean. Drake asked to be dressed in his armour, and was buried at sea in a lead coffin off Portobelo. Divers still look for it.

death.label: Ponce de León died at Havana, July 1521
death.text: A Calusa arrow struck his thigh on his 1521 attempt to colonise south-west Florida, and he died in the first week of July, probably of infection, soon after the expedition sailed to Havana, Cuba, where the page and its infobox place his death; he was buried in Puerto Rico.

death.label: Juan Garrido died in Mexico City, between 1547 and 1550
death.source: NPS, Juan Garrido: from legal documents
death.text: NPS dates his death between 1547 and 1550 from legal documents; Wikipedia says about 1550, in New Spain. His burial place is unknown.
